graph_decision.evidence: J1 (index 500) shows a sharp drop in all three axes with sustained offset; J2 (548) shows a smaller opposite-signed jump that does not fully recover the J1 offset, and the trajectory continues with a new baseline—indicating J1 is a permanent step. J3 (612) shows another sharp drop in all axes, again not recovered afterward, confirming a second permanent step. No clear shift-and-return pattern exists across any candidate pair: P1 fails because post-J2 displacement remains offset from pre-J1; P2 fails because J3 is a further drop, not a return; P3 fails because J2→J3 is a drop, not a recovery. Thus, J1 and J3 are standalone permanent steps; J2 is a transient spike or minor offset but not part of a recoverable transient—however, since it does not form a clean return with either J1 or J3 and the post-J2 level is not restored to pre-J1, it must remain unpaired. Per instructions, retain standalone step IDs only when persistent abrupt changes remain: J1 and J3 qualify; J2 does not represent a persistent step (its offset is partially reversed by later motion but not fully restored to original baseline), so it is not a standalone step. Hence only J1 and J3 are retained as steps; no pairs selected.
